zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 休市固定收益簡報

美國固定收益市場依SIFMA建議於Labor Day休市，沒有新的美國現券收盤價。假日期間，伊朗表示與阿曼正接近達成荷姆茲臨時航道協議，為緩解能源短缺提供可能途徑；但船舶仍受威脅，沙烏地能源設施也傳出遭攻擊，實際通行尚不確定。

官方資金流同樣改變重新開市的背景。日本披露創紀錄單月外國證券減持，一名支持再通膨的政府顧問將下一次日本央行升息預測提前至9月；印度則回收大量異常充裕的流動性。除了通膨，這些變化也會影響政府債需求，歐洲較弱的生產與房市則提供謹慎緊縮的理由。

企業仍能融資，但條件不同。REC在徵求投標後完成印度首筆據報代幣化債，Uber準備首次歐元發債，Reliance規畫大型本地交易。Bathla只取得特定專案及兩週營運資金，Cerba貸款人則考慮出售困境曝險。重點是新的資金安排，不是再泛論一次信用市場是否開放。

## 全球利率、信用與主權發展

### 荷姆茲談判提出航道，供應尚未恢復

伊朗發言人Esmail Baghaei表示，與阿曼協商已進最後階段，包括臨時安全航道。空載卡達LNG船正返回波斯灣方向，可能準備恢復出口；但德黑蘭仍警告阿曼沿岸攻擊風險，沙烏地紅海石油設施遭襲報導也威脅另一條路線。Kpler記錄前10日平均每天僅10艘商品船通過荷姆茲，5月以來最低。

供應中斷讓中介商獲利，燃料使用者卻仍困難。彭博取得的財務資料顯示，Gunvor截至6月的六個月獲利增644%，Mercuria截至6月的九個月增122%。期間不同，不能當成同一產業增速，但可見交易獲利與實體供應不足能同時存在。

### 歐洲產出弱，投資人信心卻改善

德國7月工業生產減1.1%，市場原估增0.1%。汽車減9.2%，汽車協會歸因於數週停產；風力與太陽能支持能源生產增4.7%，建築增0.9%。萊茵河低水位可能干擾8、9月，經濟學家則預期工廠訂單轉強要到第4季才帶動產出。

投資人看得更遠。歐元區Sentix由0.9升至5.1，高於2.0預估，連續第五升、2022年2月以來最高。現況由−8.0改善至−3.3，預期增3.5點至13.8。德國由−11.9升至−2.8，連續第四升、2025年7月以來最好。1,052名回覆者包括209家機構。信心改善沒有改寫7月生產下滑，卻使疲弱活動之外多了不同訊號。

德國還面臨如何把借款化為投資。薩克森－安哈特選舉後，Friedrich Merz表示聯盟須改善合作、維持目標；Ifo估計去年原供支出的新增債務，95%卻填入一般預算缺口。斯圖加特將2026年營業稅預估降至€7億，2023年紀錄曾逾€16億，並採2009年以來首份緊縮預算。地方削支可能抵銷中央刺激。

€5,000億投資計畫有憲法基礎，須三分之二多數才能推翻。UniCredit的Andreas Rees預期改革被稀釋或延後，而非癱瘓。債務占GDP 64%仍有借款空間，但2027年規畫逾€2,000億新增債務，也讓執行成效更重要。

英國財相John Healey首次重要演說重申財政紀律，並與Andy Burnham方向一致，提議透過國家財富基金及英國商業銀行帶動區域投資。這些貸款可作金融資產，在2029/30年度債務下降規則下抵銷借款，債息卻仍計入。措施包括£1.5億支持北部成長企業、增加地方保留所得稅，以及2029年前減少25%企業規管，並非大型新增支出方案。

經濟支持並不一致。Jaguar Land Rover計畫最多裁4,000人。Lloyds報告8月房價年減0.4%，2023年11月以來首降，市場原估增0.2%；月減0.2%，而非預估增0.1%，7月又由增0.1%修正為減0.1%。Capital Economics認為，典型兩年固定房貸利率可能由7月4.8%走向9月5%。Nationwide卻報告年增1.6%、月增0.2%，另有招聘調查顯示全職聘僱增加。

法國Jordan Bardella承諾反對提高家庭與企業稅，縮窄少數政府財政整頓選項。Jean-Luc Mélenchon因衰退風險批評歐洲央行緊縮，並未提出已達成的新債務取消安排。Bardella也主張對烏克蘭援助採更有對價的關係；這些仍是政治立場，不是已實施措施。

烏克蘭則面臨具體融資條件。IMF訪問團告知議員，低於€150、約$175的進口包裹加值稅，在法案首讀失敗後，不應期待獲豁免。2026年赤字逾$320億，審查中的堅定立場關係到預算與社會給付能否繼續獲資金。

### 日本儲備減持，印度已實際回收資金

日本財務省週一資料顯示，8月外國證券減少創紀錄$878億，接近近期匯率干預規模。分析師推測可能出售包括短天期美債來支持日圓。減持是已知資料，工具及目的卻是推論，不能據此認定日本民間投資人全面退出外債。

高市早苗顧問、Credit Agricole日本首席經濟學家Takuji Aida將下一次升息預測從2027年1月提前至9月，認為10月初臨時國會前有機會。他預計1月前再升一次，之後約每半年一次。這名知名再通膨支持者轉變，顯示政府周邊阻力可能減少；片山皋月仍重申決策屬日本央行。停損與選擇權交易商賣美元，也參與假日匯率變動。

紐約聯準銀行研究提供官方分散配置的背景。美元儲備占比由十年前64%降至去年56%，但Linda Goldberg與Sneha Parthasarathy發現，2015年後兩段期間，增加與減少美元的國家數大致相同。中國與俄羅斯主導2015至2019年多數主動分散；2019至2023年則加上墨西哥、摩洛哥。其他國家的匯率管理與美元流動性需求仍重要。6月另一研究發現普遍長期分散意向，但意向不是已完成交易。

印度9月7日吸收逾₹6兆、$635.3億。銀行在目標₹7兆的30日操作投入₹2.59兆後，隔夜再放入₹3.53兆。五名交易員將較弱長天期參與歸因技術問題，一名熟悉操作者卻否認，表示所有投標均經e-Kuber通過。因此不能確定是銀行主動拒絕回收流動性。9月6日體系資金曾達₹11.6兆，接近存款4%。

六名銀行人士估計，截至9月4日一週央行至少賣$80億美元，最高估$150億，一人估$100億至$110億、至少前週三倍；賣美元也會回收盧比。異常盈餘源於避險優惠吸引逾$1,360億海外借款與外幣存款。央行回收已逾₹8.5兆，IDFC First Bank另提出市場穩定計畫債券與賣出後買回交換等可能工具。選哪種方式，會決定下一輪透過新增政府券供給，還是外匯及貨幣市場進行。

### 保險新資本與AI投資帶動不同資金流

中國先前宣布的增資方案，如今披露五家國有保險公司共獲CN¥700億，其中China Life為CN¥350億、China Taiping為CN¥70億；PICC擬向財政部配售至多CN¥150億A股。特別債首次用於保險，延伸原先支援銀行工具。GMF Research估計，四家商業保險取得CN¥600億可容納約CN¥1,000億新增股票曝險，資本改善未必全轉成買債。

8月外匯儲備另由$3.419兆增至$3.438兆，高於$3.425兆預估。當月美元轉弱影響估值，增額本身不能辨認新買資產。

馬來西亞8月政府與公司債吸引$39億外資，創2016年資料開始以來紀錄。RBC的Abbas Keshvani連結到出口及資料中心直接投資。馬國也評估以Huawei Ascend 910C晶片用於RM20億、約$4.94億主權AI計畫，由Telekom Malaysia營運。華府警告可能違反出口規則；馬國稱這是商業選擇，並討論另一標案讓Nvidia更直接競爭。Huawei尚未獲最後選定，決策可能影響支撐目前流入的美國投資關係。

澳洲AI建設則先帶來成本問題。Bloomberg Economics的James McIntyre估計，資料中心資本支出2026至2027年可能逾GDP 2%，與住宅、基礎建設及再生能源爭奪熟練建築勞工。CreditorWatch的Ivan Colhoun認為，材料與薪資壓力，使弱房市對貨幣政策的解釋力不如平常；生產力效益可能晚於施工需求。

### 企業融資前進，困境債權人選擇保留哪些曝險

Uber委任Goldman Sachs、BNP Paribas、Bank of America、Deutsche Bank與Morgan Stanley準備可能的五檔歐元首發，固定利率3、6、8、12與20年，接續歐洲擴張及已同意的$148億Delivery Hero收購。美國企業與金融發行人今年已售近€1,250億、創紀錄速度，Uber金額與價格仍未定。

MTN在十年未國際發債後，由Absa、Bank of America、Citigroup與MUFG安排倫敦會議，明確為非交易路演，公司稱是財報更新。它表示有能力償還10月剩餘$5億境外債；擬以約$22億買入尚未持有的IHS Towers股份，另有部分舉債需求。接觸投資人提供選項，並不證明有再融資缺口。

REC完成₹50億、$5,290萬代幣化債，2028年5月到期、票息7.30%，已不只是先前徵求投標。約20名投資人使用央行數位貨幣，據報包括HDFC Bank、ICICI Bank、Axis、Yes Bank、AK Capital Services、ICICI Securities Primary Dealership、Taurus Group及Trust Investment Advisors。Taurus與AK確認參與；HDFC只確認安排，未確認買入。證券與數位央行付款結合，可加速分配與交割，但尚未證明次級交易更深。Reliance Industries另準備至多₹1,250億、$13億本地債，可能成為今年印度最大上市交易。

Bathla管理人Teneo與五家貸款人同意提供兩週有限營運的緊急支持。知情者估約A$400萬，Teneo未確認金額；只有參與貸款人的工程繼續，其他專案暫停，約213名員工停止工作。相對A$34億欠款，這保護特定專案，不是資助全體完工，更長期支持仍需廣泛協議。

Cerba則有一家或多家銀行尋求出售€4.5億循環額度中的約€2,800萬，協調程序正接近。這些較少交易的債權可能由關係銀行轉至重整專業投資人。相對約€50億債務金額不大，卻是債權人調整曝險的新跡象，而非又一次重整公告。

## 下一個開市日觀察

荷姆茲實際船流持續增加、攻擊減少，才能讓伊朗與阿曼安排對燃料使用者有意義。加拿大9月8日預定對數百種美國產品課15%至50%關稅，也增加成本風險。9月10日歐洲央行決策與美國PPI、11日CPI，將檢驗壓力；歐洲預期升25個基點至2.5%，對後續而言更重要的是第二輪效應判斷。非能源繼續降溫，才有較多空間區分燃料衝擊與持久本地通膨。

日本公布儲備減持後，美國財政部9月8日3年、9日10年標售提供需求證據。投標弱會增加官方出售及企業競爭供給的疑慮，有序承接則減輕這種解讀。9月17日至18日日本央行會議再檢驗Aida提前升息的預測，不能先假定日本投資組合已調整。

烏克蘭稅務委員會主席Danylo Hetmantsev表示，政府計畫9月7日重提包裹加值稅，下一週再闖國會。通過可滿足明確IMF條件，再次失敗則即使全球能源與債市改善，融資仍不確定。

臨時航道要能安全通行，才會緩解能源短缺。德國生產下滑、投資人信心卻改善，英國房價指標分歧，烏克蘭則面臨明確IMF包裹稅條件。

日本儲備證券減少$878億是已知資料，出售美債支應干預則是推論。印度已從討論轉為實際回收，但資金盈餘仍在。

REC完成代幣化債，Uber與Reliance準備發行，MTN舉行非交易會議。Bathla支持僅限特定專案及兩週，Cerba銀行考慮降低循環額度曝險。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Holiday Fixed-Income Brief

US fixed-income markets were closed for Labor Day under SIFMA's full-close recommendation. There was no new US cash-bond close. During the holiday, Iran said talks with Oman were nearing an agreement on a temporary Hormuz shipping route, offering a possible way to relieve energy shortages. Continued threats to vessels and reports of attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure left actual passage uncertain.

Official flows also changed the backdrop for reopening. Japan disclosed a record monthly reduction in foreign securities, and a reflationist adviser brought his next BOJ hike forecast forward to September. India drained a substantial part of its exceptional liquidity surplus. These developments affect government-bond demand alongside inflation, even as weaker European production and housing provide reasons for caution on further tightening.

Companies continued to find financing, but on different terms. REC completed India's first reported tokenized-note transaction after soliciting bids; Uber prepared a euro debut and Reliance a large local sale. Bathla obtained money for only selected projects and two weeks of operations, while Cerba lenders considered selling distressed exposure. Those are new funding decisions, rather than another broad verdict on whether credit markets are open.

## Global Rates, Credit, And Sovereign Developments

### Hormuz talks offer a route, not yet restored supply

Iranian spokesman Esmail Baghaei said Oman negotiations were in their final stages, including a temporary safe route. Empty Qatari LNG tankers were returning toward the Gulf, potentially positioning for exports. Tehran nevertheless warned of attack risk near Oman's coast, and reports of strikes on Saudi Red Sea oil infrastructure threatened another route. Kpler recorded only 10 commodity ships a day through Hormuz over the previous 10 days, the lowest since May.

The disruption has rewarded intermediaries even as fuel users struggle. Financial data seen by Bloomberg showed Gunvor profit up 644% in the six months through June and Mercuria up 122% in the nine months through June. The different periods are not a common industry growth measure, but show how trading gains can coexist with physical supply constraints.

### Europe's weak output contrasts with improving confidence

German industrial production fell 1.1% in July versus an expected 0.1% gain. Autos dropped 9.2%, which the German Automotive Association attributed to a multi-week shutdown; energy production rose 4.7%, helped by wind and solar, and construction gained 0.9%. Low Rhine water could disrupt August and September, while economists expected stronger factory orders to lift output only in Q4.

Investors looked further ahead. Euro-area Sentix rose to 5.1 from 0.9, above the 2.0 forecast, its fifth increase and highest since February 2022. Current conditions improved to −3.3 from −8.0 and expectations rose 3.5 points to 13.8. Germany climbed to −2.8 from −11.9, its fourth gain and best since July 2025. The 1,052 respondents included 209 institutions. Better expectations do not reverse July's output decline; they do complicate an otherwise weak activity picture.

Germany's challenge is also to turn borrowing into investment. After the Saxony-Anhalt election, Friedrich Merz said the coalition must work better while keeping its objectives. Ifo estimated that 95% of new debt earmarked for spending last year filled regular-budget holes instead. Stuttgart cut its 2026 trade-tax projection to €700 million from a 2023 record above €1.6 billion and adopted its first austerity budget since 2009. Local retrenchment can offset national stimulus.

The €500 billion investment program is constitutionally anchored and requires a two-thirds majority to unwind. UniCredit's Andreas Rees expected reform dilution or delay, not paralysis. Debt of 64% of GDP leaves room to borrow, but more than €200 billion planned for 2027 puts greater weight on delivery.

John Healey's first major speech as UK chancellor reaffirmed fiscal discipline and alignment with Andy Burnham. He proposed using the National Wealth Fund and British Business Bank to mobilize regional investment. Their loans count as financial assets against borrowing for the 2029/30 debt-falling rule, although debt-service costs still count. Measures included £150 million for northern scale-ups, greater local retention of income tax and a 25% reduction in business regulation by 2029—not a large new spending package.

The economy offers mixed support. Jaguar Land Rover plans up to 4,000 job cuts. Lloyds reported August house prices down 0.4% annually, the first fall since November 2023 versus a forecast +0.2%. Monthly prices fell 0.2% rather than rising 0.1%, and July was revised from +0.1% to −0.1%. Capital Economics saw typical two-year fixed mortgage rates approaching 5% in September from 4.8% in July. Nationwide, by contrast, reported +1.6% annually and +0.2% monthly, while a separate recruitment survey showed increased full-time hiring.

In France, Jordan Bardella pledged to oppose household and business tax increases, narrowing a minority government's consolidation options. Jean-Luc Mélenchon attacked ECB tightening over recession risks, not a new debt-cancellation agreement. Bardella also sought a more transactional approach to Ukraine support. These remain political positions rather than enacted measures.

Ukraine faces a specific funding condition. An IMF mission told lawmakers not to expect an exception for VAT on imported parcels below €150, or $175, after the bill failed its first reading. With a 2026 deficit over $32 billion, the review's firm stance matters to continued budget and social-payment funding.

### Japan's reserve reduction and India's completed cash drain

Japan's foreign-securities holdings fell a record $87.8 billion in August, Monday's ministry data showed, near the scale of recent currency intervention. Analysts inferred sales—including shorter Treasuries—to fund yen support. The reduction is observed; its instruments and purpose are inferred, and it does not establish a broad private-investor exit from foreign bonds.

Takuji Aida, a Takaichi adviser and Credit Agricole's chief Japan economist, advanced his next BOJ hike forecast from January 2027 to September, seeing an opening before early October's extraordinary parliamentary session. He expected another by January and roughly semiannual moves afterward. The prominent reflationist's change suggests less resistance near government, though Satsuki Katayama reiterated BOJ authority. Stop-losses and options dealers' dollar selling also contributed to currency activity during the holiday.

A New York Fed study puts official diversification in perspective. Dollar reserve share fell to 56% last year from 64% a decade earlier, but Linda Goldberg and Sneha Parthasarathy found roughly equal numbers of countries adding and reducing dollars in two periods since 2015. China and Russia drove most active diversification in 2015–19; they, Mexico and Morocco accounted for much in 2019–23. Exchange-rate management and dollar-liquidity needs mattered elsewhere. A June study found widespread long-run intentions to diversify, which are not the same as completed transactions.

India absorbed more than ₹6 trillion, or $63.53 billion, on September 7. Banks placed ₹3.53 trillion overnight after ₹2.59 trillion in a 30-day operation targeting ₹7 trillion. Five traders blamed weak term participation on technical problems; a person familiar with the operation disputed that and said all bids passed through e-Kuber. The shortfall cannot confidently be read as banks rejecting sterilization. System liquidity had reached ₹11.6 trillion, near 4% of deposits, on September 6.

Six bankers estimated RBI dollar sales of at least $8 billion in the week through September 4, with estimates up to $15 billion; one put them at $10 billion–$11 billion, at least three times the prior week. Those sales withdraw rupees too. The exceptional surplus followed more than $136 billion of overseas borrowing and FX deposits attracted by hedging incentives. RBI withdrawals had exceeded ₹8.5 trillion; IDFC First Bank identified Market Stabilisation Scheme bonds and sell-buy swaps as further possibilities. The instrument choice determines whether the next drain adds government-paper supply or operates through FX and money markets.

### New insurer capital and AI-related investment flows

China's previously announced recapitalization now includes details for five state insurers receiving CN¥70 billion, including CN¥35 billion for China Life and CN¥7 billion for China Taiping. PICC plans up to CN¥15 billion of A-shares for the finance ministry. This is the first special-bond financing for insurers, extending the bank-support tool. GMF Research estimated CN¥60 billion for four commercial insurers could allow around CN¥100 billion of additional equity exposure; stronger capital need not all become bond demand.

August FX reserves separately rose to $3.438 trillion from $3.419 trillion, beating $3.425 trillion consensus. Dollar weakness affected the valuation backdrop, so the increase alone does not identify new purchases.

Malaysia attracted $3.9 billion into government and corporate bonds in August, a record in data starting in 2016. RBC's Abbas Keshvani linked demand to exports and data-center FDI. Malaysia is also evaluating Huawei Ascend 910C chips for a RM2 billion, or $494 million, sovereign-AI project operated by Telekom Malaysia. Washington warned that using them could breach export rules. Malaysia calls the choice commercial and is discussing another tender that could let Nvidia compete more directly. No Huawei selection is final; the decision could affect US investment relationships supporting current inflows.

Australia's AI buildout presents a nearer-term cost problem. Bloomberg Economics' James McIntyre estimated data-center capex could exceed 2% of GDP in 2026–27, competing with housing, infrastructure and renewables for skilled construction labor. CreditorWatch's Ivan Colhoun said pressure on materials and wages makes weak housing less informative for policy than usual. Productivity benefits may arrive later than construction demand.

### Corporate funding advances, while distressed lenders choose their exposure

Uber mandated Goldman Sachs, BNP Paribas, Bank of America, Deutsche Bank and Morgan Stanley for a possible five-part euro debut: fixed-rate 3-, 6-, 8-, 12- and 20-year maturities. It follows European expansion, including an agreed $14.8 billion Delivery Hero purchase. US corporate and financial issuers have already sold nearly €125 billion this year, a record pace; Uber's size and price remain unset.

MTN held London meetings arranged by Absa, Bank of America, Citigroup and MUFG after a decade without international issuance. The explicitly non-deal roadshow was described as an earnings update. MTN says it can repay the remaining $500 million foreign bond due October; the proposed roughly $2.2 billion purchase of the IHS Towers shares it does not own creates a separate need, partly to be debt-funded. Outreach provides an option, not proof of a refinancing shortfall.

REC completed ₹5 billion, or $52.9 million, of May 2028 tokenized notes at 7.30%, advancing beyond the earlier bid request. About 20 investors used RBI digital currency. Reported participants included HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis, Yes Bank, AK Capital Services, ICICI Securities Primary Dealership, Taurus Group and Trust Investment Advisors. Taurus and AK confirmed participation; HDFC confirmed arranging but not buying. Linking securities to digital central-bank payments can speed allotment and settlement, without yet proving deeper secondary liquidity. Reliance Industries is separately preparing up to ₹125 billion, or $1.3 billion, of local bonds, potentially this year's largest listed Indian deal.

Bathla administrator Teneo agreed emergency support with five lenders for two weeks of limited operations. A person familiar put it near A$4 million; Teneo did not confirm the amount. Only participating lenders' construction continues; other projects are suspended and about 213 employees stopped work. Against A$3.4 billion owed, this protects selected projects, not completion of the group. Longer support still needs broader agreement.

At Cerba, one or more banks are seeking to sell about €28 million of a €450 million revolver as conciliation approaches. The relatively infrequently traded claims could move from relationship lenders to restructuring specialists. The sale effort is small against roughly €5 billion of debt, but is new evidence of creditor repositioning rather than a new restructuring announcement.

## Next Open-Session Watch

Actual Hormuz throughput and fewer attacks would make an Iran-Oman arrangement meaningful for fuel users. Canada's scheduled September 8 tariffs of 15%–50% on hundreds of US products add another cost risk. The ECB decision and US PPI arrive September 10, CPI September 11. The expected ECB quarter-point move to 2.5% matters less for further pressure than its judgment on second-round effects; continued non-energy moderation would leave more room to distinguish the fuel shock from persistent domestic inflation.

Treasury's September 8 three-year and September 9 ten-year auctions provide demand evidence after Japan's reserve disclosure. Weak bidding would increase concern about official sales and competing corporate supply; orderly demand would limit that reading. The September 17–18 BOJ meeting then tests Aida's accelerated forecast, rather than any assumption that Japanese portfolios have already shifted.

Ukraine tax-committee chair Danylo Hetmantsev said the government planned to resubmit parcel VAT on September 7 for another parliamentary attempt the following week. Passage would meet a specific IMF condition; another failure would prolong funding uncertainty even if global energy and bond markets improved.

A temporary route could ease energy shortages only if safe passage resumes. German production fell despite improving investor confidence, while British housing indicators diverged. Ukraine faced a firm IMF parcel-tax condition.

Japan's $87.8 billion reserve-securities reduction was observed; Treasury sales to fund intervention were an inference. India's completed withdrawal moved beyond the prior sterilization discussion, though surplus cash remained.

REC completed tokenized notes, while Uber and Reliance prepared sales and MTN held non-deal meetings. Bathla support covered only selected projects and two weeks; Cerba banks considered reducing revolver exposure.
